inconsistencies: #34038 and #35387 solve the same problem (make trace logging usable, expose it over the logging RPC) by different routes; reviewers should settle #34038 first, as #35387's own discussion names it as the competing alternative.

#35355 (ajtowns) re-does the -loglevel/-trace deprecation and logging RPC schema change from #34038 on top of an atomics refactor; the two by the same author must not land independently, review #34038 first and rebase #35355 on the outcome.

#36384 migrates RPC argument parsing to self.Arg<> across node and wallet RPCs and subsumes #34950, which does the same for generatetoaddress alone; #36384 should be reviewed first and #34950 closed or rebased as a subset.

#36503 (reject assumeutxo rollback without tip data) and #36266 (fail dumptxoutset early on stale targets and concurrent runs) both rewrite dumptxoutset's precondition checks and will conflict; review #36503 first since it prevents a crash.

#35728 changes GetTransaction/TxIndex to throw on I/O and index errors, and #36002 builds pruned-txindex error reporting on the same code path; #35728 is the prerequisite in spirit and should be reviewed first.
#36200 and #36204 both close HTTP worker/slot exhaustion vectors on the same server; they are complementary, not alternatives, but #36200 is the trivially triggerable one and is banded higher.
#36124 and #36159 are sequential refactors of the same HTTPRemoteClient/HTTPRequest code by one author; reviewing them out of order will produce conflicts.
#10102 (multiprocess) states dependence on #29409 and unblocks #19460/#19461; none of those are in this category, so its rpc-side position here understates its project role elsewhere.
result.notes: The category is dominated by a long P3 tail of single-method additions and diagnostics. I kept the bands as assessed except #35054, and ordered P3 so that returned-data and error-reporting bugs precede new fields and methods, which the category explicitly ranks above additions with no external consumer. Logging PRs (#34038, #35387, #35355) are logging-first and kept adjacent because their only rpc stake is the shared logging RPC schema change.
